A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hypo3D benchmark. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical content, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original foundation-model and human evaluations on Hypo3D, including experiments on reference frames, relevant and irrelevant context changes, and scene alignment.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds GPT-based scoring and experiments on prompting, in-context learning, multiple views, and caption quantity.

M1.justification: The benchmark-construction pipeline, anchor-based world frame, and main inference guidance remain unchanged. v3 describes the existing Figure 11 prompt as Chain-of-Thought; this is not a newly introduced method component. Alternative prompts are evaluated as controls.

E1.justification: Both versions use 700 indoor scenes, comprising 500 ScanNet and 200 3RScan scenes, with 7,727 changes and 14,885 question-answer pairs. Task categories and irrelevant-change scenarios remain intact. Added experiments vary inputs and procedures within this coverage; Table 7's other datasets are literature comparisons.

E2.justification: The foundation-model and human comparator sets in corresponding experiments are retained. New prompting and input studies use existing models as ablations. GPT-4o-mini supplies evaluation scores rather than becoming an additional evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends evaluation with GPT-4o-mini grading on a normalized 1–5 scale, simplified-prompt controls, three-shot in-context learning, five-view versus top-view inputs on 50 sampled scenes, and 30/50/100/200-caption conditions. The original zero-shot EM/PM evaluation and listed inference hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Sections B.3.3–B.3.6 test whether task decomposition, demonstrations, additional viewpoints, or richer captions alleviate model difficulties. These address several alternative explanations absent from v1. Earlier frame, alignment, context-change, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Added GPT grading is an evaluation metric, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing main and matched appendix scores are retained, but substantial new results appear in Tables 10 and 12–15. Examples include a GPT score of 46.55 for semantic-map GPT-4o, Llama3.2 scores of 23.91 without versus 26.08 with CoT, ICL-related declines, and mixed effects of additional views and captions. These are newly reported comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The formal task and object-change definitions remain unchanged. The added GPT-score equation documents normalization and averaging for an adopted evaluation metric; it introduces no new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, proofs, or theoretical properties.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution and principal performance claims in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion remain stable. However, the new Impact Statement calls Hypo3D 'the first 3D VQA benchmark,' introducing broader novelty wording than v1 and than the paper's own discussion of earlier 3D VQA benchmarks supports.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of human errors and hypotheses connecting ICL failures to inadequate example coverage, multi-view results to integration difficulties, and caption results to long-text reasoning. Existing limitations concerning textual changes, indoor environments, and object-level modifications are retained and relocated.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents XY-plane/Z-axis point-cloud alignment, the default use of 30 sampled object captions, the GPT evaluator, and the simplified control prompt. It explicitly states code/data availability and describes intended resource releases. These disclosures do not establish changes to the original implementation.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.3 and Table 7 compare Hypo3D with six existing datasets. Added references include ReferIt3D, MMScan, 3D-VISTA, OpenDlign, and Match-Stereo-Videos. This expands positioning around hypothetical changes and world frames while retaining the original related-work argument.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained, with small language edits and removal of an unfinished sentence. v3 adds acknowledgments, an Impact Statement, an appendix contents list, and quantitative subsections, while moving the unchanged limitations to the end.

P2.justification: The appendix gains dataset-comparison, GPT-score, and four ablation tables. The complete-results table is redesigned with an Input column, and existing figures and prompt panels are resized or relocated. Table 5 also acquires an incorrect alignment-experiment caption above its unchanged question-type examples.

improvement.justification: Alternative scoring and the new prompt/input ablations strengthen the evidence supporting the retained benchmark, while added technical disclosures aid reproducibility. The net gain is limited by incomplete specification of some new experiments, an incorrect Table 5 caption, and overly broad novelty wording in the Impact Statement.
